solutionSql:
WITH scanned AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT id
  FROM staging_scans
  WHERE id IS NOT NULL AND status IS NOT NULL
),
islands AS (
  SELECT id, id - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY id) AS island
  FROM scanned
)
SELECT CAST(MIN(id) AS integer) AS start_id,
       CAST(MAX(id) AS integer) AS end_id,
       CAST(COUNT(*) AS integer) AS scans
FROM islands
GROUP BY island
ORDER BY start_id;
ambiguities: An id sent twice with one copy carrying a status and one copy NULL: I counted it as carrying a status (WHERE status IS NOT NULL before DISTINCT). The revised text says an id sent twice counts once and a run needs every id to carry a status, but it does not say whether a NULL copy breaks the id. Another reading requires every copy to carry a status.
notes: Revised text: NULL ids are not counted and consecutive means one id after the previous one, both now stated, so the NULL-id ambiguity is gone. Casts: start_id and end_id were already integer; scans cast to integer (was bigint). Sample islands unchanged: 1000-1004 (5), 1006-1007 (2), 1009-1015 (7), 1017-1026 (10), 1028-1037 (10), 1039 (1). Hidden datasets gave identical output, so I did not inspect their rows for NULL ids or conflicting duplicates.
